solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: US era's, er, done for — cheer up!

indicators.note: something done for is wrecked, so the preceding words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters of US, era's and er, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A lament that the American era is over, with a stammering 'er', followed by a call to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure someone is to comfort them and restore their confidence, which is what telling them to cheer up does.

clue.text: Be an editor: dare blithely to be taken to court!

indicators.note: doing something blithely means carelessly, so the word beside it is treated without care and jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed up
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A warning to an editor that publishing carelessly could land them in court.
explanation.walkthrough: REDA from dare, then CT: REDACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to prepare text for publication by revising or censoring it, which is the job of someone working as an editor.

clue.text: (& 23dn./26dn.) Go public with press: "working on drug that might get Trump high"

parts.note: to air views is to make them public
to press is to push or force
a machine that is working is on
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A press release teasing a substance that could make the President high.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drug to get Trump stoned; 'high' really means up in the sky aboard the presidential jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The presidential aircraft carries the US President aloft, literally lifting him high above the ground.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) "Unusual screwing — cool!" — but Trump may well ruin it for May

definitions.text: but Trump may well ruin it for May

parts.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary
screwing is slang for a sexual liaison

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic comment on an unusual affair, soured by the thought of Trump spoiling things for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: May is Theresa May, the UK Prime Minister, not the month; the phrase is the name for the close tie between Britain and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the close diplomatic bond between Britain and America, which a volatile president could damage for a British leader.

clue.text: Republican to admit to suppressing article: "Bush"

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down and keep it in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to own up is to admit
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Republican admitting to hushing up a newspaper article about President Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: R, then OWN holding A: ROWAN. The quoted 'Bush' looks like George W., but it is a shrub or small tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree often growing as shrubby woody plant, so it can be called a bush.

clue.text: Disaster! Conservative right terrorist group prevails

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
R is the abbreviation for right
the jihadist group also called Islamic State

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm that a right-wing faction and a terrorist group are winning.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or calamity, close to a catastrophe or emergency.

clue.text: Place coveted by creepy Piers, made by disturbing types

definitions.note: a descriptive definition of a plural noun

indicators.note: something coveted is held close, so one piece is wrapped inside the other
creepy suggests something twisted and unsettled, so the name beside it is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A dig at Piers Morgan, a TV presenter, lusting after a position and stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan is a British broadcaster and former tabloid editor; his name is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripples are small waves or knock-on effects, the kind of stir that troublemakers cause when they disturb calm water or society.

clue.text: Imagine dismissing extreme right wing international politician's medical aid via backdoor

indicators.note: dismissing drops something, and the extreme right wing of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to imagine is to suppose
I is the abbreviation for international
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A sneer at a far-right international politician sneaking in medical help through the back door.
explanation.walkthrough: The political words pull towards a story about a party; 'extreme right wing' only means the end letter is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppository is a solid medicine inserted into the rectum, literally a treatment delivered through the back passage.

clue.text: First new European leader … then hostility

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of European

explanation.surface: A new European head of government arrives, and conflict follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First new European leader' reads as one phrase about a politician; it splits into first (scrambled) plus the leader of European.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter conflict or discord, the same idea as hostility between people or groups.

clue.text: Gallagher's intro in crappy song

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: something crappy is dire

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so just the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Gallagher

explanation.surface: A critic panning the opening of a song by Noel or Liam Gallagher of the band Oasis.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song, such as a lament sung at a funeral.

clue.text: Everything in western tabloid that gets a pasting?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other two

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
everything is all
a tabloid is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a tabloid newspaper is about to get a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pasting' sounds like a thrashing, but here it is the glue brushed on before hanging; the tabloid wraps the 'everything' word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallpaper is hung by brushing adhesive paste onto its back, so it literally receives a coat of paste.

clue.text: Replacement 'new tool' that's somewhat subdued

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a noun: a sound that is somewhat subdued

indicators.note: a replacement swaps things around, so the quoted words are reordered

parts.note: the letters of the two quoted words

explanation.surface: A replacement for a new gadget that is a bit muted.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, quiet pitch in music sounds hushed, and figuratively a low note is a dispirited, downbeat moment.

clue.text: Note: no.1 heartless Trump bill gets backing

indicators.note: backing moves things backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, keeping only the outside letters of the name

parts.note: only the first and last letters of Trump
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A memo that the top bill of a gutted Trump administration is gaining support.
explanation.definitionFit: A caption is a short piece of explanatory text attached to a picture, a brief written note.

clue.text: Mad emasculated Trump: "Here, pal, pin that on defenders of American values"

definitions.text: pin that on defenders of American values

indicators.note: mad means crazy and disordered, so the letters are scrambled
emasculated means stripped of the male, and M for male is taken out

parts.note: taken as written before the male letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unhinged, unmanned Trump handing someone a medal for patriots.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP loses M (male) to leave TRUP, which is mixed with HEREPAL. The Purple Heart is a US military decoration for soldiers wounded in service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Purple Heart is a medal pinned on US service members wounded while fighting for their country.

clue.text: My! Stinking rich!

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise
food that has gone off stinks

explanation.surface: A gasp at someone who is stinking rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinking rich' reads as one idiom; it splits into a wordplay word and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-off means having plenty of money, comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: see 3dn.
Experiment with gutted tissue fat

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of tissue
stout means fat

explanation.surface: Trying out a procedure on removed fatty tissue, like a lab trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something out is to try it in practice to see whether it works, which is experimenting with it.

clue.text: Every constitution's to lapse; nothing to prevent it's going ahead

definitions.text: nothing to prevent it's going ahead

parts.note: every is all
a constitution is a system, plus the S of 's
to lapse is to go, as a deadline goes by

explanation.surface: A grim forecast that every constitution will lapse, with nothing to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a crisis of democracy; the definition is the launch-control phrase for everything being ready.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from rocket launches, declares that every check is complete and the operation may proceed.

clue.text: Result of Conservative act that scrapes the bottom?

definitions.text: Result of Conservative act that scrapes the bottom?

parts.words: Result of Conservative act that scrapes the bottom?
parts.note: surface reading: the outcome of a Tory policy that scrapes the barrel

parts.words: Conservative act that scrapes the bottom
parts.note: setter's reading: an act of conserving that dredges up goods from the seabed

explanation.walkthrough: Conservative with a capital C suggests the Tory party, but it means preserving; scraping the bottom is the seabed, not the barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is property rescued from a wreck, often recovered by dredging the sea floor, so it is saved goods.

clue.text: Fiasco, having sex out of bed

parts.note: screw is slang for sex
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A disaster involving sex somewhere other than the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-up is a slang term for a bungled mess or blunder, just like a fiasco.

clue.text: Political party, despicable sort — agree?

parts.note: Con is short for the Conservative Party
a cur is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Asking if the reader agrees that a political party is full of despicable people.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a formal word for agreeing.

clue.text: A first for Donald: past fancy 'suits'

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the word is reworked
a first for a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Donald
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Donald Trump, a novelty in office, with a past taste for fancy suits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' sits inside the indicator phrase and is also kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapts, as a verb, means alters something to fit, the same as suits in 'suits it to the purpose'.

clue.text: Tragedy to back arse-licking publication

indicators.note: to back up is to move backwards, so the little word is turned round

parts.note: the word to, turned round
Hello! is a British celebrity magazine known for fawning coverage

explanation.surface: Deploring that someone would support a sycophantic magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, about a Moorish general destroyed by jealousy.

clue.text: Raided euro finally gets rather ragged protection

indicators.note: protection wraps around and shields, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something rather ragged is frayed

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of euro

explanation.surface: Raiders find the euro worn out and in need of protecting.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside FRAYED after its first letter: F-O-RAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To foray is to make a sudden raid or attack into enemy territory, so forayed means raided.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Daily Mail's no. 2: cert to dissipate moral qualities

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun: character is the sum of them

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner, also called a char

indicators.note: to dissipate is to scatter, so the letters are dispersed and regrouped
number two picks out the second letter

parts.note: the second letter of Mail
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that the Daily Mail's second in command is a sure bet to squander morals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British tabloid, but the clue splits it: a daily is a char (a cleaning woman) in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's character is the set of moral traits, such as integrity and honesty, that defines them.

clue.text: How unlikely hero Trump finally makes you cry

indicators.note: unlikely suggests things not in their expected order, so the word is reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so just the last letter of each of the two words is kept

parts.note: the final letter of hero
the final letter of Trump

explanation.surface: Reflecting that seeing Trump as an unlikely hero would make you weep.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud shout of excitement, a kind of cry or yell.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Gone off Balls and his coveted score?

parts.note: balls is slang for nonsense
ten is the top mark a judge can give on Strictly Come Dancing

explanation.surface: Recalling former Labour minister Ed Balls on the TV dance show Strictly, hoping for top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls, an ex-minister, competed on Strictly Come Dancing, a BBC ballroom contest scored out of ten per judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has decayed and spoiled, which is to say it is putrid.

clue.text: Abandoned, he sells out, securing Trump's end

indicators.note: securing holds something fast inside, so one piece goes within the other
out suggests something put out of order, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of Trump

explanation.surface: Someone deserted who sells out while making sure Trump's downfall happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpless means unable to fend for oneself, the state of someone abandoned, as in helpless or abandoned laughter.
